title: DUET: Distilled LLM Unlearning from an Efficiently Contextualized Teacher
claim: Before the intervention the model's top prediction is a confident domain-specific answer; afterward refusal and uncertainty tokens dominate and the target-knowledge token drops out.
layout: 2 vertically stacked bar charts (before on top, after below), shared color legend, value labels above bars, rotated token labels
description: Two stacked bar charts show the top-10 next-token logits for a Harry Potter query. The top panel, 'DUET Before Distilled Unlearning', has one tall red 'Answer' bar (Harry, 16.05) that towers over the other tokens at about 9.5–10.7. Those are blue 'Refusal Words' bars (None, none) and pale yellow 'Other Words' bars (Although, Eleven, However, Yes, and others). The bottom panel, 'DUET After Distilled Unlearning', has no red bar. Blue refusal tokens (None 11.79, Unfortunately, unknown, Unknown) now sit at or near the top, with yellow tokens like Let and Please between them. The y-axis is 'Logits Value'. Each panel has the same legend in the top right, and the numeric value is printed above each bar. The eye goes first to the tall red bar at top left. The crop also shows a cut-off 'Top-K Logit Distillation' heading and stray large glyphs along the left edge.
caption: Top-10 logits for a Harry Potter related query before and after DUET unlearning. Multi-token words are shown complete for clarity. Before unlearning, domain-related and affirmative tokens dominate. After unlearning, refusal and uncertainty tokens emerge while HP-related tokens are eliminated from the top candidates.
abstract: LLM unlearning is a technique to remove the impacts of undesirable knowledge from the model without retraining from scratch, which is indispensable towards trustworthy AI. Existing unlearning methods face significant limitations: conventional tuning-based unlearning is computationally heavy and prone to catastrophic forgetting. In contrast, in-contextualized unlearning is lightweight for precise unlearning but vulnerable to prompt removal or reverse engineering attacks. In response, we propose Distilled Unlearning from an Efficient Teacher (DUET), a novel distillation-based unlearning method that combines the merits of these two lines of work. It learns a student model to imitate the behavior of a prompt-steered teacher that effectively refuses undesirable knowledge generation while preserving general domain knowledge. Extensive evaluations on existing benchmarks with our enriched evaluation protocols demonstrate that DUET achieves higher performance in both forgetting and utility preservation, while being orders of magnitude more data-efficient than state-of-the-art unlearning methods.
